h1:
Chiang Mai vs Pai
which to choose?
intro: Torn between Chiang Mai and Pai? Here is an honest, side-by-side comparison so you can pick the one that fits your trip — or fit both in.

blocks.html: Short answer: It is less either/or — Pai is a popular add-on from Chiang Mai. Chiang Mai is a complete city (temples, cafés, food, nightlife) and a great base; Pai is a small, chilled mountain town (hot springs, sea of mist, a canyon) about 3 hours away over 762 curves. Most base in Chiang Mai and add 2–3 nights in Pai.

blocks.text: Chiang Mai vs Pai at a glance

items: Pick Chiang Mai if you want a complete city — temples, cafés, food, nightlife and rooms for every budget — as a northern base
Add Pai if you want a chilled mountain town with hot springs, mist and a slow pace
Doing both is best — base in Chiang Mai, then add 2–3 nights in Pai (bring motion-sickness pills for the 762 curves)

faq.q: Should I add Pai to a Chiang Mai trip?
faq.a: If you have time and like a chilled mountain vibe, yes — Pai is about 3 hours from Chiang Mai by minivan and suits 2–3 nights. With limited time or if winding roads make you carsick, Chiang Mai alone still offers plenty.

faq.q: How are Chiang Mai and Pai different?
faq.a: Chiang Mai is a big city with temples, cafés, food and nightlife, used as a northern base, while Pai is a small mountain town focused on chilling, hot springs, mist and nature — fewer sights but a lovely vibe.

faq.q: What is the road to Pai like?
faq.a: It is a mountain road of 762 curves, about 3 hours by minivan from Chiang Mai — scenic but very winding, so if you get carsick, take medicine beforehand and sit near the front.
